attributes.protocol: Predicted ddG compared with experimental ddG in kcal/mol; PCC Pearson and SCC Spearman correlation.
limitations: Developer comparison (ThermoMPNN authors).

name: Megascale held-out test split ddG prediction (Dieckhaus et al. 2024 Table 2)
description: RMSE and correlation of predicted against experimental ddG on the Megascale held-out test split.

attributes.protocol: Predicted ddG compared with experimental ddG in kcal/mol; PCC Pearson and SCC Spearman correlation.
limitations: Developer comparison: the authors built ThermoMPNN and chose the comparator set (methods with readily accessible code).
Megascale proteins are 40-72-residue domains, many de novo designed, measured by one proteolysis assay over a narrow ddG range (-3 to 5 kcal/mol).
RaSP and PROSTATA were retrained on Megascale data for this table; other comparators use their published training.
No uncertainty is printed in Table 2 (Table 1 ablations give seed SD for ThermoMPNN only).

name: S669 direct ddG prediction (Dieckhaus et al. 2024 Table 3)
description: RMSE and correlation of predicted against experimental ddG on the S669 direct.

attributes.protocol: Predicted ddG compared with experimental ddG in kcal/mol; PCC Pearson and SCC Spearman correlation.
limitations: Most rows are compiled from Pancotti et al. 2022 (reference 30); the S669 values here are not an independent rerun.
ThermoMPNN was trained on a homologue-filtered Megascale set for this column (footnote *); ABYSSAL was scored on 420 filtered variants (footnote dagger).

The ACDC-NN RMSE printed here (1.60) disagrees with the source it cites: Pancotti et al. 2022 Table 1 prints 1.49 for the direct variants with the same Pearson 0.46, and 1.60 is DDGun3D's value there. That result is disputed; the citation '(30, 36)' also points at an unrelated reference 36.
No uncertainty is printed.

name: Ssym direct and inverse ddG prediction (Dieckhaus et al. 2024 Table 3)
description: RMSE and correlation of predicted against experimental ddG on the Ssym direct and inverse.

attributes.protocol: Predicted ddG compared with experimental ddG in kcal/mol; PCC Pearson and SCC Spearman correlation.
limitations: Most rows are compiled from earlier publications (references 29 and 30 and the methods' own papers) rather than rerun by the authors.
Variant counts are not printed in Table 3.
No uncertainty is printed.

The Results text says homologues of both Ssym and S669 were removed from the Megascale training set before ThermoMPNN was retrained for Table 3, but only the S669 ThermoMPNN cells carry footnote *; whether the Ssym values use the filtered model is not stated.

name: S669 direct and reverse ddG prediction (Pancotti et al. 2022 Table 1)
description: Pearson r, RMSE and MAE on direct, reverse and all variants, plus antisymmetry r and bias, for 21 predictors.

attributes.protocol: Each tool run once on S669 and its reverse variants with default parameters (web server or stand-alone); predicted ddG compared with experimental ddG in kcal/mol.
limitations: Single benchmark of 669 variants with reverse variants built from modelled structures.
Several methods were developed by authors of this paper: ACDC-NN, ACDC-NN-Seq, DDGun and DDGun3D, and, through P. Fariselli and E. Capriotti, INPS3D, INPS-Seq, I-Mutant3.0 and I-Mutant3.0-Seq.
Predictor versions and servers are listed only in the Supplementary Materials, which were not read; web servers may have changed since.
Proteins are under 25% identity to S2648 and VariBench, but predictors trained on other data (for example ThermoMutDB itself) may still overlap.
No uncertainty is printed.
Direct-variant correlation alone misleads: MAESTRO has the highest direct Pearson (0.5) but a reverse Pearson of 0.2 and a bias of -0.57 (Table 1).

name: Relevance of S669 direct and reverse ddG prediction (Pancotti et al. 2022) to "Assess methods for protein stability experiments"
description: Experimental ddG for proteins dissimilar to the usual training sets directly tests how well each predictor ranks substitutions by folding stability on unseen proteins, and the reverse variants test for bias towards destabilising predictions.

attributes.endpoint: Pearson r, RMSE and MAE of predicted against experimental ddG for 21 predictors on 669 direct and 669 reverse variants, with antisymmetry
attributes.rationale: Experimental ddG for proteins dissimilar to the usual training sets directly tests how well each predictor ranks substitutions by folding stability on unseen proteins, and the reverse variants test for bias towards destabilising predictions.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator before citing a result.
Do not combine this mapping's evaluations with any other protocol's results; datasets, splits, structures and predictor versions differ between sources.
limitations: Single benchmark of 669 variants with reverse variants built from modelled structures.
Several methods were developed by authors of this paper: ACDC-NN, ACDC-NN-Seq, DDGun and DDGun3D, and, through P. Fariselli and E. Capriotti, INPS3D, INPS-Seq, I-Mutant3.0 and I-Mutant3.0-Seq.
Predictor versions and servers are listed only in the Supplementary Materials, which were not read; web servers may have changed since.
Proteins are under 25% identity to S2648 and VariBench, but predictors trained on other data (for example ThermoMutDB itself) may still overlap.
No uncertainty is printed.
Direct-variant correlation alone misleads: MAESTRO has the highest direct Pearson (0.5) but a reverse Pearson of 0.2 and a bias of -0.57 (Table 1).
